This is the single most important thing this tester established beyond the diff doc's own evidence: the diff doc's §0 explicitly states the dedicated post-deploy probe (s1-probe.js via zz-crm-probe-spec-shapeA) is UNRUN and blocked, leaving the deployment status of the CRM half formally unproven at build time. This tester's live clone executions supply that missing live-envelope evidence directly: spec_asked appears on the wire on every spec-domain response (SR-13, SR-2, SR-14, SR-15, SR-8, SR-7, SA-4, SA-5), the S4/DEV-1 Matched-on VALUE upgrade renders correctly (bowl count: 2, not bare 'bowl count'), the DEV-1 brand-verbatim exemption is PROVEN against real catalogue data (SR-14b: 'brand: BRAVAT', not titlecased 'Bravat' -- resolving the diff doc's stated open item), and D7 junk suppression is confirmed deployed (SR-8: zero SORENTOBAG/SORENTO188/junk). The dedicated zz-crm-probe-spec-shapeA proxy remains blocked (s0-blocked-first case file) and its more rigorous contract-shape checks (S1-C counterweight, exhaustive unrecognized_terms/field-type checks) remain formally UNRUN -- this tester's evidence is real but narrower in scope than what s1-probe.js would prove, and does not substitute for running it.
headline_finding_no_free_terms: Structurally CONFIRMED, not just reconstructed. The resolve-entity-http.jsonBody was read directly from the deployed workflow JSON (not inferred from response behaviour): the key set is exactly {query, match_mode, tokens, allowed_entity_types, access_levels, domain, fallback_to_all_types, limit, spec_fallback, understand_phrase} -- no free_terms key anywhere. Every response's via_token field independently corroborates this dynamically: it carries the FULL raw customer sentence (e.g. 'double bowl kitchen sink with thickness 1.2mm'), not just the entity raw a pre-migration free_terms-based body would have sent.
headline_finding_dev1_brand_exemption: PROVEN, not INCONCLUSIVE. SR.md's own SR-14 prompt ('do you have wall hung basin') did not surface a brand key on this catalogue slice, which would have left DEV-1 formally untested per the diff doc's own caveat. This tester fired a second, minimal probe ('show me bravat wall hung basin') that DID surface brand:'BRAVAT' in matched_specs, and the rendered reply showed '_Matched on: brand: BRAVAT and mounting: Wall Hung._' -- BRAVAT rendered verbatim uppercase, genuinely differing from what a blind titlecase pass would have produced ('Bravat'). This is a real, discriminating, live-data proof.
headline_finding_sa5_deviation: FLAGGED FOR THE REVIEWER, NOT A FAILURE. SA-5 ('SRTWC286 and wall hung basin') pre-migration was documented as a 'known v1 gap': the descriptive half was expected to be silently dropped, leaving only the code answer. Post-migration, BOTH halves resolve and render in ONE merged 15-item list (10 code-prefix products + 5 spec_search products), via the same SR-9 third-shape mechanism (AND-zero-intersection -> OR-fallback -> per-token resolution UNION a query-keyed spec_search resolution) that SR-9/SR-15 already proved reachable for a code+nonexistent-code pair. This appears to be a positive behaviour change (the customer gets more information, not less) but it is a functional deviation from SA.md's documented contract fact #1 ('REPLACE, never merge ... the renderer NEVER sees a mixed set') that the reviewer should explicitly sign off on, the same way SR-9's finding required a documented amendment to the coder's reachability table. See spec-raw-text-migration-SA-5-20260815.json for full detail.
